Changes made

- inventory.py
  - Added a reservations map (self.reserved).
  - Implemented reserve(sku, qty), release(sku, qty), and fulfill_reservation(sku, qty).
  - Kept remove_stock(sku, qty) semantics (checks on-hand quantity).
  - Changed available(sku) to return on-hand minus reserved.

- orders.py
  - create_order now atomically checks availability for all items and reserves them. If any line lacks stock, it raises InsufficientStock and nothing is reserved.
  - cancel now releases reservations for pending orders.
  - fulfill converts reservations into on-hand deductions via Inventory.fulfill_reservation.

Notes and reasoning

- Inventory.available(sku) now reflects on-hand minus reserved as requested.
- Reports (low_stock, stock_value) continue to read inventory.stock (on-hand), so their behavior is unchanged.
- remove_stock still checks and deducts only on-hand stock as before; fulfilling uses fulfill_reservation to both release the reservation and deduct on-hand stock.
- Reservation operations validate quantity > 0. release and fulfill_reservation raise errors if asked to operate beyond reserved quantities.

I ran the existing unit tests (with Python's unittest) — all tests pass. If you'd like, I can add tests for reservations (e.g., creating an order with insufficient available stock raises InsufficientStock and leaves inventory unchanged), or adapt error types/messages to match any external expectations.
